title: Purifying Organic Compounds Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A tea strainer keeps the leaves back and a naphthalene ball shrinks without melting. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (Chapter 8, Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques) Diya sees that every kitchen trick uses one difference, and chemists purify new compounds the same way.

You will see the five methods matched to the property they use: sublimation (camphor, naphthalene), crystallisation (hot solvent, filter, cool, activated charcoal), and a live distillation on the molecule bench where chloroform (334 K) boils off from aniline (457 K). Then fractional distillation (crude oil), distillation under reduced pressure (glycerol from spent lye), steam distillation with p1 + p2 = p, differential extraction in a separating funnel, and chromatography: adsorption (silica gel, alumina, column and TLC), partition (paper) and the Rf value. A worked Rf example, the exam trap, an original JEE Main pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

This is Episode 86 of our PUC Chemistry series. 

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.
